text:
With Nathan MacKinnon out about a month and Cale Makar about two weeks (Field Level Media), Martin Necas is the player Colorado leans on most up front, and he took a hit in Utah on Wednesday that Yahoo Sports listed among several injury scares in a rough first period. His status is the thing to watch.

He has 24 points in 22 games, 10 goals on 6.2 expected. That's shooting 22% against 18% last season, and it usually cools. His last 10 games have been quieter: 8 points against 10.5 expected, which tracks with the top line losing its center.

That line, Artturi Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Necas, had outscored opponents 20-10 together. Evolving-Hockey had Necas at 3.4 wins above replacement last season, 11th among forwards, with the caveat that his teammates rated in the 99th percentile, which flatters anyone. This month answers the question that caveat raises: what does he look like as the man driving the line instead of riding with the best player in the world? Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he has the tools, a 62% carry-in rate and strong setup passing.
headline: Necas is the Avalanche's top line now
